hooks.text: An astronaut claimed his lunar golf shot went for miles.
The most famous golf drive on the Moon was a flop.
One astronaut hit a forty-yard golf shot on the Moon.

title: The Moon Golf Shot That Wasn't Miles Long
description: Apollo 14 commander Alan Shepard famously hit golf balls on the Moon, but high-resolution photo analysis revealed his drive was much shorter than he claimed.

beats.text: An astronaut claimed his lunar golf shot went for miles.

queries: Alan Shepard golf shot Apollo 14 TV frame

beats.text: Apollo 14 commander Alan Shepard attached a six-iron to a tool.
beats.visual: photograph of the modified Wilson six-iron club head at the USGA Museum, 2020

beats.text: His rigid spacesuit made a standard stance impossible.
beats.visual: photograph of Alan Shepard standing on the lunar surface during EVA, 1971
queries: Alan Shepard Apollo 14 lunar suit photo

beats.text: So Shepard had to hit two balls using one hand.
beats.visual: lunar surface photo of footprints and golf ball impression in dust, 1971

beats.text: On live television, he boasted his shot flew miles and miles.
beats.visual: television screen broadcast image of astronaut standing near equipment cart, 1971
queries: Apollo 14 live TV broadcast lunar surface

beats.text: NASA photo analysis later measured the actual landing spot.
beats.visual: high-resolution orbital photograph of the Apollo 14 landing site, 2021
queries: Apollo 14 landing site high res orbital image

beats.text: His second drive really traveled just forty yards.
beats.visual: enhanced archival photo showing location of golf balls on Moon surface, 2021
queries: Apollo 14 golf ball location photo analysis

beats.text: Yet nobody else has ever hit a golf ball on another world.
